description: MAP_CONSTRUCT(key, value ...) - the one member of the family that BUILDS a map, every expectation measured live. Members come out KEY-SORTED rather than in argument order, and the result is a MAP the rest of the family can read. An odd argument count is rejected naming the next EVEN count ("expected 4, got 3") rather than a maximum, and fewer than two arguments is an arity error. A NULL LITERAL is rejected in either half ("Function MAP_CONSTRUCT does not support NULL argument type"), but at RUN TIME - measured over a multi-row table so no all-NULL column could be folded to a literal - a NULL key DROPS the pair while a NULL value is kept as a JSON null. The KEY half refuses BOOLEAN, DATE and VARIANT while the VALUE half takes all three, a duplicate key is an error, and a semi-structured value is kept whole. Converted 1:1 from functions/MapConstructTest (now retired); MAP cells are read directly, which renders identically on the engine and over HTTP, while the ARRAY-valued MAP_KEYS is read through TO_JSON.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE mcn (id INTEGER, k VARCHAR, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO mcn VALUES (1, 'a', NULL), (2, NULL, 1), (3, 'b', 2)
SELECT MAP_CONSTRUCT(k, v) FROM mcn WHERE id = 1
SELECT MAP_SIZE(MAP_CONSTRUCT(k, v)) FROM mcn WHERE id = 1
SELECT MAP_CONSTRUCT(k, v) FROM mcn WHERE id = 2
SELECT MAP_CONSTRUCT(k, v) FROM mcn WHERE id = 3
